deck: HOW 192 PRACTITIONERS BUY TRAFFIC, ROUTE LIVE CALLS THROUGH RTB RING TREES, AND RESELL THEM AT A SPREAD
TRACKING NUMBERS, IVR PRE-QUALIFICATION, TCPA CONSENT, BUYER NETWORKS, AND THE UNIT ECONOMICS OF SCALING
site_ui.lead: Learn how working operators price, route, and resell live inbound calls, from a $50 call that nets a $15 margin and a 40% broker markup to ring trees with minimum-revenue floors and an 8-second billing buffer.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies on inbound pay-per-call and RTB ping-post arbitrage, from platform setup and IVR design to TCPA compliance, verticals, network building, and unit economics. Every claim, metric, pro-tip, and quote carries timestamped inline attribution to its source video.

Unit Economics, Call Quality, and Scaling Case Studies
flow: Weigh pay-per-call against pay-per-lead and affiliate networks against direct clients, then read every line of the offer: minimum call length, buyer hours, hold period, and who owns the buyer.
Price the gap between traffic cost and call payout with at least a 40% markup, and model the worst-case paid ratio before you spend.
Assign unique tracking numbers per publisher and put your own number in front of the network's so you can verify every call and catch skimming.
Set eligibility filters on geo, hours, caps, and concurrency, add a minimum-revenue floor with static fallback targets, and prefer SIP when the buyer accepts it.
Add an 8-second latency buffer over the buyer's billable duration and run real test calls that confirm tracking, routing, answer, timing, and recording end to end.
Send paid traffic only after testing, keep publisher IDs and your margin hidden from buyers, and capture consent records to limit TCPA exposure.
